p: Thinking of going? A bit of prep makes the scares more fun and the queues less painful. Turn up a little before your timed slot so there's no panic at the door, and travel light, as you'll be moving through narrow, dimly lit sets and big bags just get in the way. Shoes you can walk comfortably in are a must; this is a standing, shuffling sort of attraction rather than a sit-down show.

The experience runs as a sequence, so you can't skip ahead or hang back once your group sets off. That's part of the magic, but it does mean it's worth a toilet stop before you start. Photography rules can be strict inside to protect the surprises, so expect to keep your phone in your pocket for most of it and just enjoy the madness.

If someone in your group is nervous, the back of the crowd is the safest place to be. Fancy a starring role? Shuffle to the front and make eye contact with the actors. You'll regret it in the best way.

Because it sits inside County Hall, it pairs brilliantly with a walk along the Queen's Walk riverside path, a ride on the London Eye next door, or a wander over Westminster Bridge for the classic Big Ben photos once you've escaped back into daylight.
